claim.text: A well-initialized dense neural network contains globally minimal solutions that can retain the prior class knowledge while providing room to learn the new class knowledge through isolated fine-tuning of the networks or subnetworks.

The convergence analysis considers a convex-Lipschitz loss function $f$ with gradient norm bounded by $\rho$, i.e., $\|\boldsymbol{v}_t\|\le \rho$ for per-iteration gradient vectors $\boldsymbol{v}_t$, and an update rule $\boldsymbol{w}^{(t+1)}=\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\eta\boldsymbol{v}_t$ applied sequentially over $T$ steps; with $\boldsymbol{w}^*$ any comparator vector, for any $B_m< B_p < B$, where $B_m=\|\boldsymbol{w}_m^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$ with $\boldsymbol{w}_m$ denoting the effective weighted parameters when masks $\boldsymbol{m}$ are applied, $B_p=\|\boldsymbol{w}_p^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$ with $\boldsymbol{w}_p$ denoting the prompt-only effective parameters (with $\boldsymbol{m}=\mathbf{1}$), and $\|\boldsymbol{w}^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\| \le B$, choosing $\eta=\sqrt{B^2/(\rho^2 T)}$ yields the bound $$ \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\langle \boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*,\boldsymbol{v}_t\rangle \le \frac{B_m\rho}{\sqrt{T}} < \frac{B_p\rho}{\sqrt{T}} < \frac{B\rho}{\sqrt{T}}. $$

The convergence analysis considers a convex-Lipschitz loss function $f$ with gradient norm bounded by $\rho$, i.e., $\|\boldsymbol{v}_t\|\le \rho$ for per-iteration gradient vectors $\boldsymbol{v}_t$, and an update rule $\boldsymbol{w}^{(t+1)}=\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\eta\boldsymbol{v}_t$ applied sequentially over $T$ steps; with $\overline{\boldsymbol{w}}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}$, $\boldsymbol{w}^*$ any comparator vector, and $B_m=\|\boldsymbol{w}_m^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$ where $\boldsymbol{w}_m$ denotes the effective weighted parameters when masks $\boldsymbol{m}$ are applied, the sub-optimality $f(\overline{\boldsymbol{w}})-f(\boldsymbol{w}^*)$ is upper-bounded by quantities that scale as $\mathcal{O}(B_m\rho/\sqrt{T})$.

With $B_m=\|\boldsymbol{w}_m^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$, where $\boldsymbol{w}_m$ denotes the effective weighted parameters when masks $\boldsymbol{m}$ are applied, and with $\boldsymbol{w}_p$ denoting the prompt-only effective parameters (with $\boldsymbol{m}=\mathbf{1}$), a smaller $B_m$ (associated with learning soft masks) yields a tighter bound than prompt-only or unconstrained updates.
On ViT-based continual-learning benchmarks Soft-TF obtains state-of-the-art class-incremental and task-incremental results.
DualPrompt-Soft-TF on 10-Split-CIFAR100 achieves ACC = 97.87% and Forget = 0.21;
on 20-Split-CIFAR100 ACC = 99.05% and Forget = 0.24;
on 10-Split-ImageNet-R ACC = 82.38% and Forget = 0.59.
The results of DualPrompt-Soft-TF using Gradient ID substantially outperform prompt-only baselines and rehearsal/regularization baselines on 10-Split-CIFAR100.
(DualPrompt with Prompt ID: ACC=86.50%, Forget=5.77)
(; L2P-PGP: ACC=84.34%, Forget=5.59)
(BiC with 5,000 exemplars: ACC=81.42%, Forget=17.31)
(; EWC: ACC=47.01%, Forget=33.27)
Soft-TF generalizes to vision-language backbones
. On 10-Split-CIFAR100 with CLIP backbone, CLIP-Prompt-Soft-TF-L[1-12] using Gradient ID attains CIL ACC = 85.90% and Forget = 3.07, and TIL ACC = 96.83% and Forget = 0.44
(CLIP with Prompt ID: CIL ACC=73.76%, Forget=5.60; CLIP-PGP: CIL ACC=79.47%, Forget=4.23) under the same task settings.
Applying Soft-TF to higher transformer layers yields stronger continual-learning performance in DualPrompt settings, producing near-zero forgetting.
(DualPrompt-Soft-TF-L[10,11,12] Gradient ID ACC = 97.87%, Forget = 0.21)
Fine-tuning only attention projections (QKV and projection matrices) at last layers already attains very high performance.
(ACC = 97.17%, Forget = 0.40 in one configuration)
Attention modules are highly influential for task-adaptive specialization.
Extending WSN-style subnetworks to pre-trained transformers yields competitive sparse solutions.
DualPrompt-WSN-L[10,11,12] with sparsity c=87.0% on 10-Split-TinyImageNet achieves ACC=91.91% and Forget=0.38.
Dense pretrained transformers contain high-performing sparse subnetworks.
Soft-TF generalizes to CLIP.
Applying Soft-TF to layers L[10,11,12] yields stronger continual-learning performance in DualPrompt settings, producing near-zero forgetting.
Fine-tuning Soft-TF-L[12] w/ only ATTN already attains very high performance.

note.text: elaboration of claim 1: when starting from a well-pretrained (well-initialized) transformer backbone, there exist per-task subnetworks or task-adaptive soft-networks that (i) preserve previously learned classes and (ii) admit isolated fine-tuning to learn new classes without catastrophic forgetting.
